words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as a connected return, not as an isolated scene. The connector can be heard as resumption or coordination, so the prose should keep the boundary alive: the concealed well-scene has moved into public arrival, but the particle itself does not explain the brothers' motive. Because it is fused to {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}), the transition is visually and audibly carried straight into the arrival verb.

topics.reason: QAC allows either coordinating or resumptive force for the opening connector, so the exclusive labels must be narrowed to a connected boundary function rather than one fixed subtype.

words.prose: {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}) makes the brothers appear only as a plural verb ending: the group arrives, but no individual is named. Its perfect form completes the motion before the ongoing weeping of {{ar:يَبْكُونَ}} ({{tr:yabkūna}}), so the ayah moves from a bounded entrance to a prolonged display. The local sequence starts with arrival, then gives the father, then nightfall, then tears, setting up the spoken claim in the next ayah (12:17). The local syntax gives {{ar:أَبَاهُمْ}} ({{tr:abāhum}}) as the reached father, so any 'bringing' or 'presenting' sense must stay as narrative shadow: the fabricated account and shirt are not a separate local object in this word. The long ā and medial hamza make the sound catch before the plural ending, fitting arrival as motion that stops in presence. Within Surah 12, this first deceptive arrival before the father looks ahead to answering arrivals and restorations (12:93-96; 12:100).

topics.headline: unnamed plural arrival as completed public action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the brothers become a collective grammatical action rather than named individuals, and that their arrival is complete before the tears continue.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect 3mp with pro-drop subject agreement, and the following imperfect circumstantial clause supports the completed-arrival versus ongoing-weeping contrast.

words.prose: {{ar:أَبَاهُمْ}} ({{tr:abāhum}}) makes the father definite through the brothers' own suffix: he is not introduced by name, but as their father. The noun-five accusative shape, with its long ā case-marking, makes him the reached endpoint of {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}), and the suffix binds the unnamed plural subject to the person they are about to deceive. The broader father/ancestor range is narrowed here to the immediate household relation, while still letting the father stand as the vulnerable origin-point to which the sons return. Later Surah 12 scenes answer this deceived father-position with restored parental honor (12:100).

words.prose: {{ar:عِشَاءًۭ}} ({{tr:ʿishāʾan}}) is not a decorative timestamp. As an indefinite accusative time adverb, it folds the evening hour directly into the arrival without a preposition and carries the ayah's only explicit timing, making this rare adverbial deployment structurally exposed. The selected sense is evening or nightfall, but the {{ar:ع ش و}} ({{tr:ʿ-sh-w}}) field also includes dimness and weak night-sight, so the father's reception is staged under constrained seeing. Its canonical extended form lets the evening word linger and then catch at the hamza before the ayah moves into weeping. The evening side also stands alone here, without the morning counterpart of morning-evening formulae (19:11; 19:62). That pressure is strengthened by the word's middle position between {{ar:أَبَاهُمْ}} ({{tr:abāhum}}) and {{ar:يَبْكُونَ}} ({{tr:yabkūna}}): the father is reached, the light drops, and the audible tears close the scene.

topics.reason: The local sense remains temporal, but V4 accepts nightfall and weak-sight branches for the root, so the perception payoff survives as controlled coloring rather than a replacement sense.

words.prose: {{ar:يَبْكُونَ}} ({{tr:yabkūna}}) is the ayah's landing. As an imperfect circumstantial verb, it means the brothers came while weeping: the tears are simultaneous with the arrival and still unfolding after the perfect {{ar:جَاءُوا}} ({{tr:jāʾū}}). The plural ending keeps the same unnamed group onstage, now as emotional signalers before their father. Because the verb has no explicit object, the grief is displayed without saying whether it is over Yusuf, the story, or the performance itself, and the wording reports observable crying without proving sincerity. The Form I surface casts them as weepers rather than as makers of someone else weep, even though the same surah later turns the grief onto the father (12:84; 12:86). The arrival is framed by overt grief rather than restrained modesty (28:25), and the word occupies the weeping side of the laugh-weep polarity (53:43). Within the sparse local grief-root field, the proper-name branch remains outside the sense, so the rarity sharpens the verbal display without importing sacred-place meaning.

topics.headline: ongoing circumstantial weeping
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that weeping is not a later event but the manner in which the brothers are arriving, still in process at the ayah's close.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence explicitly marks the final verb as a circumstantial clause describing the arrival subject, and QAC supplies imperfect 3mp form.

topics.headline: observable crying without stated object

topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence give no explicit object, and the rows' sincerity caution is not contradicted by the local form.

topics.headline: weepers, not grammatically causers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the surface grammar lets the brothers wear the role of sufferers while the narrative keeps pressure on the grief they will cause.
topics.reason: The causative idea is narrowed because the local surface is Form I imperfect; it survives only as contrast with an absent causative derivative and with later narrative effect.

topics.headline: performed tears turn toward the father
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the brothers' performed tears become the seed of the father's later destructive grief in the same surah (12:84; 12:86).
topics.reason: The source rows give concrete same-surah references, so the echo is preserved as directional narrative pressure.

topics.headline: weeping pole and arrival-manner contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this arrival is framed by overt grief rather than restrained modesty, and that the weeping occupies one side of the Quranic laugh-weep polarity (28:25; 53:43).
topics.reason: The comparisons are retained as contrastive echoes with concrete references, not as governors of the local grammar.

topics.headline: final word makes tears the landing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes on the audible emotional display, setting up the brothers' spoken claim in the next ayah (12:17).
topics.reason: The final circumstantial verb is the last word of the ayah and directly precedes the next ayah's speech opening.

topics.headline: sparse grief verb, not sacred-place import
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local grief verb is distributionally exposed within a small root field, while the proper-name branch is kept outside the local sense.
topics.reason: The root's proper-name branch is accepted in V4 but is not the local IV verbal use; the distributional rarity survives without importing sacred-place meaning.

topics.headline: proper-name adjacency cannot govern the verb

topics.reason: The row's structural coincidence overreads the root inventory. The proper-name branch may be noted as separated, but it should not shape the local prose for {{ar:يَبْكُونَ}} ({{tr:yabkūna}}).

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Dim time and manufactured tears cooperate as evidentiary cover.** ع ش و B004/B001 (evening; dim clarity) and ب ك ي B004 (forced or feigned crying) are structurally compressed into one short arrival scene. I infer that reduced visibility helps performance substitute for inspectable fact. The ayah reads as staging: time, affect, and approach are coordinated.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:18 shifted verification from dim affective performance to the visible shirt, correcting tears with material evidence.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Weeping used as evidential sound.** The variants under `ب ك ي:B001` jointly specify grief, tears, and vocal lament. The terse ayah supplies crying before the brothers state their claim in 12:17, while 12:18 supplies the manufactured blood and the father rejects their description. The packet gives affect first and evidence second; I infer that the display is meant to pre-load the report with credibility. *Yabkūn* therefore reads as a performed evidential channel whose sound cannot establish the event asserted.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:84-86 distinguishes Jacob's embodied grief and directed complaint from this performed weeping, showing retrospectively that tears acquire evidentiary value only through their relation to truthful disclosure.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, dalın temelini karanlık ve bir şeyin seçilemez hale gelmesi olarak doğrular. facets.statement: Karanlık, bir şeyin görünürlüğünü ve açıklığını azaltır.

Gün batımından sonraki gece namazı ve gün batımıyla gecenin koyulaşma vaktini birlikte anan adlar bu zaman alanına bağlıdır.
